flags.headline: US-Iran Hormuz conflict escalates further over the weekend; US Fifth Fleet's Bahrain base confirmed damaged
flags.detail: Escalation continues from the Sept 6-11 pattern of tit-for-tat tanker/missile strikes. New this weekend: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said Iranian forces heavily damaged the US Fifth Fleet's base in Bahrain, leaving the USS Abraham Lincoln's crew without a place to pull in. Also new: a possible diplomatic opening -- Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said the Strait of Hormuz will reopen if the US ends its naval blockade, and Arab-state foreign ministers are due to meet Iran's FM Monday in Salalah, Oman to discuss a temporary shipping arrangement. No ceasefire yet. Energy-sleeve price reaction has stayed muted/mixed through Friday's close (VLO +2.17%, OKE +0.27%, CVX +0.28%, DVN -0.87%, CNX -1.65%) despite the escalation, consistent with the pattern since early September.
flags.thesis_link: Matches DVN key_risk: 'Oil and gas price volatility remains the dominant swing factor for earnings and free cash flow ... could reverse quickly given global supply dynamics.'

evidence.source: Al Jazeera -- 'US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?'
Wikipedia -- '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis' (secondary aggregation of primary wire reporting on the Bahrain base damage and Pezeshkian statement)

flags.headline: Peripheral-vascular supply constraints continue; management reaffirms FY26 guidance
flags.detail: No new developments since the Sept 8 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference disclosure. Confirmed via follow-up reporting: the constraint traces to Stryker's post-cyberattack peripheral-vascular manufacturing shutdown -- the smaller vascular business is taking longer than other segments to rebuild capacity, dragging growth by 70-80bps in both Q2 and Q3 with the same drag expected into Q4. Hip sales also softer, particularly in Europe. Management held full-year 2026 organic growth guidance at 8.3-9.3% despite this. Price roughly flat Friday (-0.78% to $267.81), still trading near its recent 52-week low set on the disclosure. Not a clean citation match to a specific listed key_risk (closest is the 'organic growth deceleration below the 8.3% guidance floor' valuation-reset risk) so thesis_link is left unset rather than overclaiming a direct hit.

evidence.source: MedTech Dive -- 'Stryker stock falls on slower peripheral vascular, hip sales'
TIKR -- 'Stryker Stock Drops Over 7% As Supply Chain Constraints Impact Peripheral Vascular Business'
